steps.text: Place potatoes in a large pot and cover with salted water; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-low; simmer until almost tender, about 15 minutes. Add cod and continue to cook until cod and potatoes are tender, about 5 minutes more.
Drain; transfer to a large bowl. Add egg, butter, onion, and parsley; mash until well combined. Form into four patties.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add patties and cook until golden brown, 3 to 5 minutes per side. Drain on paper towels and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Cod Fish Cakes
raw_recipe.description: This cod fish cakes recipe, with flaky white cod, potatoes, onion, butter, and parsley, is delicious because they're crispy outside and moist inside.
raw_recipe.name: Cod Fish Cakes

review.reviewBody: This is a good recipe,similar to the Bermuda Cod Fish Cake recipe, for added flavour add 1/2 Tbs of crushed fresh thyme or dried Thyme, season to taste using black pepper, seasoning salt & garlic powder. Chill the mixture in the refrigerator for an hour, this will blend the flavors and solidify mixture to avoid crumbling when frying. Before frying coat in seasoned flour mixture (white flour, seasoning salt, black pepper and paprika, this will ensure a nice crispy coating and no crumbling. For perfect even cakes, try using an ice-cream scoop to form balls and shape with hands.

Since we like a lot of flavor, I used this as a base recipe and doctored it up a bit. Also, I like to use up what's on hand. Here's what I did and they were delicious! Thanks for the idea. Used red potatoes, added minced red bell pepper, green onion (instead of the minced onion), chopped baby spinach, and of course salt and pepper. I coated the cakes in a mixture on panko and parm cheese and let them sit in the fridge to set up for about 30 minutes. I then sautéed them in about 2 tbsp evoo in a cast iron skillet on the grill. WAY healthier than the amount of oil called for and they were quite crunchy. For a dipping sauce, I whisked sour cream, horseradish, Dijon mustard, and capers. Hope you enjoy them as much as we did..
Very good, I just added a little extra seasonings. Made them into patties, rolled them in panko, put them in the fridge for an hour, seared them in hot oil and then finished them off in the oven.

I used leftover baked potato in this recipe, so I mashed that up in a bowl, added the cod which I had fried in butter, then fried onions and a garlic clove, then added some green onion to that at the end to wilt it. Didn't have any parsley so added thyme. Added all that to my potato/fish mixture and mashed. Scooped it out into 1/3 cup portions (which made 8 cakes), rolled in masa corn flour, then fried in olive oil. It was good, my son who claims he does not like cod went back for a second fish cake. I used one small and one large potato as I only had a 400g package of cod (which is 54g less than a pound), didn't need the egg to hold it together.

Looking at the ingredient list, I knew these cakes were going to be bland. So, I decided to add my own touch to the recipe.. 1st of all, I seasoned the fish with some salt, Old bay seasoning and garlic powder and broiled it( much better flavor, this way). Then added some more of the same spices to the mushed potatoes before adding the flaked fish to them. Last, I used some Panko bread crumbs on both sides of the fish cakes for crunchier outside. i Also, I made this prep in the morning and refrigerated the fish cake till diner time. This way the cakes were firmer and were easy to handle while frying.

Outstanding. It's always difficult to get my 12 year old son to eat fish, but we all loved this recipe. I did follow many suggestions. I had two pounds of cod (we had none leftover) so I used 6 small russet potatoes. I added a 1/2 teaspoon of dried thyme, oregano, garlic powder, onion salt 1/2 teaspoon of old bay seasoning , 2 teaspoons of hot sauce, and 1/2 cup of bread crumbs. I doubled all the ingredients in the recipe except for the butter which I kept at 1 tbs. The only change I will make the next time, is to add 3/4 cup of bread crumbs, as a few of the cakes fell apart. I might also try to make one large flat cake. As well I only let the potatoes cook (once the water was boiled) for 10 minutes and allowed the fish to cook in the boiling water for another 10 minutes. I fried them approx. 5 minutes a side. If I see with the extra bread crumbs that they are firm enough I will attempt to BBQ them which will cut down on the amount of oil required. Enjoy!!!

Good recipe but a bit bland for my taste. I added some finely chopped onion (along with the grated) as well as some Old Bay (a necessity for Marylanders when it comes to seafood, lol!). I tried frying in a small amount of oil and the cakes were fine. But they were even better after I lightly coated them with flour before frying. This recipe was made using 1/2 the ingredients - half of an egg was 1 tablespoon of beaten egg). I'd make this again.

I changed the recipe by frying the onions until they were crispy and brown and added red pepper as well. Added sesame seeds browned to the mixture. Added celery (dehydrated) salt and pepper and garlic powder and one egg. Fried it,but it fell apart. The recipe needs bread crumbs added..probably panko crumbs would work well.

The next time that I make the fish cakes I'll use the quisinart to blend the raw fish, add the cooked potato add scallions and onions bread crumbs..about a cup with the potatoes and then it will be a great recipe.
Like others I added S&P and old bay. I recommend chilling them before frying and coating patties with bread crumbs.

I read several of the reviews so I used thyme, red pepper and a bit of paprika. I added some panko crumbs. I put the bowl in the freezer while I got the rest of the dinner fixed and the dishes done. I coated mine in a mix seasoned flour and corn meal so they'd be a bit crispy. Everyone enjoyed them.

I used thyme, salt, pepper, and fresh garlic. I added a glove of garlic to the boiling potatoes and fish. And added the thyme salt and pepper to mashed mixture. It was delicious! This recipe is a good base for fish cakes leaving it open to add whatever spices you prefer. I also used flounder instead of cod. Yum!
Easy recipe and a great way to use left over mashed potatoes.

As at least one other reviewer commented, this is a very easy and delicious recipe, but a little bland. You can, however, season the fish/spud mush to taste before adding the egg. I used about 3/4 teaspoon of Old Bay, which woke it right up. There are a few more seasonings I'd like to try; maybe sea salt, lemon pepper, and dill. I'll definitely make this again.
It was easy to make. I added more seasoning because I like things spicy. It came out really good.
Scallions instead of opinion and added rock fish .
Definitely add as much seasoning as you can to pump up the flavor but the idea is good. Cooling it before frying does help, as does dredging it in panko. Will make again
just add some of my secret seasoning
I made it and it’s really good I like it. I just add a little bit salt, pepper and smoked paprika. Thank you for the recipe.

I made this recipe tonight and the cod fish cakes turned out great. I did tweek it a little with grated lemon, garlic along with the grated onion. As for seasoning I added old bay and a little crushed peppers. I totally enjoyed making as well as eating them. I am planning on doubling this recipe to freeze for future meals. The cakes along with a chef salad make the perfect meal.
I made the codfish cakes. They turned out great!
